chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ibrahim ibn Isḥāq ibn Ibrahim from Abdillah ibn Hammād al-Anṣārī from Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAmmār and Abdillah ibn Bukayr from Abū ʿAbdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said, 'It is not permissible to give zakat less than five dirhams, for that is the minimum amount of zakat.'

As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ṣuhbān who said: I wrote to al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible for me, O my master, to give a man from my brothers two dirhams and three dirhams from the zakat, as that has become confused for me?' So he wrote, 'That is permissible.' This is applicable to the nisab that follows the first nisab, because the second and third nisab and what is above that, perhaps two dirhams and three dirhams are sufficient according to the increase in wealth, so there is no harm in giving that to one person. As for the first nisab, that is not permissible in it according to what we have previously stated. As for that which indicates that it is permissible to give more than five dirhams.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of zakat that can be given to a single recipient according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the minimum threshold for zakat liability and the minimum valid distribution amount, establishing five dirhams as the floor for a single recipient. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves the apparent contradiction by explaining that while the primary nisab requires a minimum distribution of five dirhams, larger wealth accumulations allow for smaller, proportional disbursements to individuals, reflecting the flexibility of Shia fiqh in zakat administration. This ruling underscores the principle that zakat obligations scale with wealth, ensuring equitable support without imposing undue burden on the giver.
